prompt: In the workspace where a member posted the message pinning our GPU memory incident on a hard CUDA allocator limit (not fragmentation) and announced reverting the batch-size config, in the channel that also has Robert Chen as a member, please create a new channel called 'cuda-limit-followup' there for the hardware-scaling writeup.
binding_note: The identifying message (Priya's CUDA-limit diagnosis), its author's workspace membership, the channel containing that message, and Robert Chen's membership in that same channel must all resolve to one channel/workspace pair; RoboWorks' similarly-worded incident message sits in a different channel whose membership does not include Robert Chen, so it fails the joint condition.

roles.facts: U_PRIYA, workspace member of T01WORKSPACE, posted the message in C_INFRA concluding the OOM issue was a hard CUDA allocator limit and announcing a batch-size revert.
roles.reason: Authors the identifying message and holds the workspace membership that starts the route.

roles.facts: Message 1706001931.000000 in C_INFRA by U_PRIYA: 'it's definitely the batch size increase hitting a hard CUDA memory limit... Reverting the batch size config now.'
roles.reason: The specific diagnosis message identifying the channel.

roles.facts: C_INFRA (core-infra), team_id T01WORKSPACE, contains the identifying message and has Robert Chen (U_ROBERT) as a member.
roles.reason: Conversation node linking message to the qualifying membership.

roles.facts: U_ROBERT is a member of C_INFRA.
roles.reason: Conversation-membership condition that must hold alongside the message for the route.

roles.facts: T01WORKSPACE ('Test Workspace'), holds the workspace membership of U_PRIYA.
roles.reason: The referent workspace selected by the full route.

roles.facts: U_B_CARL, workspace member of T02BETAROBOT, posted a similarly-worded message in channel B_INFRA about GPU memory pressure and reverting a config change.
roles.reason: Superficially similar authored diagnosis but in a different workspace.

roles.facts: Message in B_INFRA by U_B_CARL: 'We hit a memory ceiling on the GPU cluster after the last config push, reverting now.'
roles.reason: Plausible decoy message resembling the diagnosis but not the target.

roles.facts: B_INFRA, team_id T02BETAROBOT, contains the decoy message; members are U_B_CARL and U_B_DANA only.
roles.reason: Lacks Robert Chen as a member, failing the conversation-membership condition.

roles.facts: U_B_DANA is a member of B_INFRA (not Robert Chen).
roles.reason: Shows the decoy channel's membership does not satisfy the identifying condition.

roles.facts: T02BETAROBOT ('RoboWorks'), holds the workspace membership of U_B_CARL and U_B_DANA.
roles.reason: Excluded workspace despite a similarly-themed message, because the membership condition fails.

obligations.name: create_followup_channel
obligations.description: Create a new channel named 'cuda-limit-followup' inside the identified workspace for the hardware-scaling writeup.
obligations.scope: ordinary channel creation scoped to the resolved workspace

obligations.name: resolve_target_workspace
obligations.description: Identify the single workspace whose member authored the CUDA-limit diagnosis message in a channel that also has Robert Chen as a member, to supply the team_id for channel creation.
obligations.scope: identification via workspace membership -> user -> message -> conversation -> conversation membership route

task_spec.text: Identify the workspace via the described member/message/channel-membership route, then create a new 'cuda-limit-followup' channel in that workspace.

access_plan: Use search.messages / conversations.history to locate the CUDA-allocator-limit diagnosis message and its author; use conversations.members on that message's channel to confirm Robert Chen's membership; use users.info on the author to obtain their workspace (team) association; then call conversations.create with the resolved team_id and name 'cuda-limit-followup'. The added RoboWorks (T02BETAROBOT) team, its B_INFRA channel, and the decoy message/members are discoverable the same way but fail the Robert Chen membership check.
